subject: Post-demo: Greenline integration follow-up + repro for embeddings 5xx
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@greenline.com>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor@greenline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 17:15:00 -0800
Subject: Great chat today — next steps and a quick integration checklist

Hi Alex / Taylor,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciated the context on your compliance workflows and the reranking use case. As promised, a short recap and proposed next steps so we can get a focused integration spike scheduled: 

- Recap: you want a hosted inference path for POC (embedding-based search + reranker), with a fallback to local/private for sensitive flows. Key constraints: sub-300ms median latency for search path, deterministic token retention policy, and SOC-2 evidence for audit.
- Immediate next steps:
  1) Greenline to share a small sample dataset (anonymized) and the exact reranker prompt(s) you plan to use.
  2) Our side will deliver an SDK quickstart and an integration repro for the embedding + reranker flow.
  3) Joint 60–90 minute technical spike next week to validate auth routing + timeout settings.

Ben — included you to help with the SDK snippets and a repro plan. Priyom — can you own the initial repro and follow up with minimal config we should try for their retrieval + rerank flow?

Alex — please ping back with a preferred time window for next week and attach one or two sample queries (anonymized).

Thanks,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai
From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@greenline.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@greenline.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 19:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps and a quick integration checklist

Hi Sofia,

Thanks — timing for next week looks good. I’ve attached a small anonymized dump (10 docs) and two example queries. We did a brief run on our side against the embedding endpoint you demoed and saw intermittent 502/5xx responses when batch size exceeded ~64 vectors; attaching the trace we captured (trace-20261128.txt).

Notes from our infra team:
- We’re using a wrapper that POSTs batches of 128 embeddings at once to /v1/embeddings.
- Typical request body ~1.2MB.
- Failures look like a backend 502 with an opaque gateway message, then client-side timeout after 10s.

Can we try the spike on Tue 2026-12-01 10:00 PT?

Alex

Attachments: greenline_sample_10.json (attached), trace-20261128.txt (attached)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@greenline.com>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor@greenline.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 00:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps and a quick integration checklist

Alex — thanks for the trace, that helps a lot. Quick notes from my side before the spike:

1) Request sizing: 1.2MB for 128 vectors sounds like a likely culprit for intermittent 5xxs at our edge gateway under burst. We recommend trying smaller batch sizes first (32 and 64) to see if the error goes away.

2) Timeouts: your client timeout of 10s is a little tight if we see GPU batching under load. For the spike, set client timeout to 30s and enable retries with exponential backoff (3 retries, base 250ms).

3) SDK snippet: attaching a minimal python snippet that shows streaming the embedding requests in 32-sized chunks and a sanity check on token/byte size. We’ll also add a server-side config to limit per-request payloads to avoid gateway memory pressure.

4) Structured output / reranker: For the reranker step, return structured scores (JSON) rather than free-text so your UI can pick top-N deterministically. We'll include an example tool-calling schema in the spike.

I’m attaching redwood-sdk-snippet.py so you can run locally; Priyom will produce a repro runbook and we’ll iterate during the Tue spike.

—Ben

Attachments: redwood-sdk-snippet.py
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@greenline.com>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor@greenline.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 02:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps and a quick integration checklist

Team — prepping the repro steps and wanted to surface technical hypotheses and the exact runbook I’ll use in the spike:

Hypotheses:
- H1: Gateway OOM/worker restart when single request payloads exceed ~1MB at peak concurrency -> 502/5xx.
- H2: Router mis-route under heavy concurrency combining streaming + sync embed calls causing backend timeouts.

Runbook (to execute Tue):
1) Reproduce locally against a staging routing pool using Greenline sample (same header auth). Run three variants: batch sizes 128, 64, 32. Capture end-to-end trace and kernel logs.
2) Toggle client timeout to 30s and record difference.
3) Enable per-request byte-limit at edge (512KB) and test with chunking on client.
4) Validate structured reranker output (JSON score array) using the provided example prompt; confirm stable top-5.

I’ll post console links/results to the Drive link (https://drive.company/shared/Greenline-Integration-Notes) during the call. Marissa — can you include procurement / MPA now that we’re moving to a spike? I’ll keep logs attached to the runbook.

—Priyom
From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@greenline.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@greenline.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 08:06:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps and a quick integration checklist

Thanks everyone — Tue 12/01 10:00 PT (your 10:00 PT) works for us. A couple quick clarifications before the spike:
- We can run client-side chunking if you recommend it; our wrapper was built for larger batches for cost reasons but we can change for the spike.
- Our security team wants to confirm that structured reranker outputs will not include PII and that we can configure deterministic retention (we prefer 0 retention for queries in production).

I’ll bring our infra lead on the call — they may ask about the per-request byte-limit and whether that requires a Dedicated pool to maintain throughput.

Taylor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@greenline.com>, Taylor Nguyen <taylor@greenline.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps and a quick integration checklist

Alex/Taylor — I’ve shared an MPA doc (greenline-mpa.pdf) to outline spike scope and standard POC terms. Regarding retention: we can offer a 0-retention option for query payloads at spike time and provide SOC-2 evidence for the hosted environment we’ll use; I’ve added the compliance contact to the Drive link.

Logistics for Tue: 10:00 PT, I’ll send calendar invite with a short agenda (repro run, auth check, retry/timeout tuning, reranker schema validation). If you prefer Dedicated to avoid edge limits, we can discuss committed-capacity pricing after the spike.

—Marissa
